question.prompt: The number of distinct solutions of the equation \(\left|x-|2x+1|\right|=3\) is

solutions.explanation:
The inner expression \(2x+1\) changes sign at \(x=-\tfrac12\). Splitting there lets us remove the absolute values using their signs.

If \(x\ge-\tfrac12\), then \(|2x+1|=2x+1\). Also \(x+1\ge\tfrac12>0\), so
\[
\left|x-|2x+1|\right|
=|-x-1|=x+1.
\]
The equation becomes \(x+1=3\), giving \(x=2\), which lies in this interval.

If \(x<-\tfrac12\), then \(|2x+1|=-2x-1\). Now \(3x+1<-\tfrac12<0\), so
\[
\left|x-|2x+1|\right|
=|3x+1|=-3x-1.
\]
The equation becomes \(-3x-1=3\), giving \(x=-\tfrac43\), which lies in this interval.

The cases are disjoint and cover every real number, with the boundary included in the first case. Each gives exactly one valid solution. Hence there are \(\boxed{2}\) distinct solutions, choice C.
solutions.title: Resolve the absolute values by sign
